create.name: Hollyhock
create.bio:
Hollyhock is a not-for-profit retreat and learning centre on Cortes Island, in the northern reaches of the Salish Sea off the coast of British Columbia. A group of ten friends bought the land in 1982 from the Cold Mountain Institute, an earlier human-potential centre run there by an Esalen-trained founder, and began hosting seminars that brought together people drawn to inner, contemplative work and people working for social and environmental change. That meeting of the personal and the public still shapes the place. The founders gave their shares away in 2008, and Hollyhock has been a registered charity ever since, with its land permanently protected.

Visitors stay for residential programmes of four to six days on a seafront campus of cabins, gardens and forest, with shared organic meals from its large kitchen garden. The yearly calendar mixes meditation and silent retreats, contemplative and nature-based practice, sacred-feminine and Indigenous wisdom work, movement and dance, creative arts and writing, and a separate leadership strand for changemakers. Guest teachers have included meditation teachers, poets, ecologists and activists. Drop-in yoga and tai chi run most mornings, the campus offers bodywork, and a few programmes travel abroad or meet online. The campus lies on land of the Klahoose, Homalco and Tla'amin peoples.

courses.title: Peru Equinox Retreat: A Journey into Balance, Renewal, and Creation
courses.description: A ten-day Hollyhock journey through Cusco, the Sacred Valley and Aguas Calientes around the March equinox, guided by Jhaimy Alvarez Acosta, a teacher of Andean wisdom traditions from Cusco. Days combine visits to sacred sites with ceremony and reflection on balance and new beginnings. Flights to Peru are not included.
courses.price: $5,800 USD ($8,250 CAD); single rooms $600 USD extra

courses.title: Awake in Our Lives: A Silent Meditation Retreat
courses.description: Five days of silent Insight Meditation on Cortes Island with Los Angeles Dharma teacher Celeste Young. Mornings work with the four foundations of mindfulness and afternoons with heart practices, alongside walking meditation, a daily Dharma talk and small-group meetings with the teacher.
courses.price: All-inclusive package (tuition, lodging and meals); price depends on accommodation and is shown at registration

courses.title: Pilgrimage to Silence: A Nature Based Retreat for Rest & Renewal
courses.description: A silent retreat on the theme of pilgrimage, led by Buddhist-Quaker Dharma teacher Valerie Brown. Practice draws on Plum Village mindfulness and Quaker worship: sitting and gentle moving meditation, Dharma teachings and long stretches of time outdoors in the island's forest and shoreline.
courses.price: All-inclusive package (tuition, lodging and meals); price depends on accommodation and is shown at registration

courses.title: Navigating Life Transitions: A Courage & Renewal® Retreat
courses.description: A Circle of Trust retreat with Valerie Brown for people at a turning point in work, relationships or later life. Quiet reflection, journalling, poetry and small circles of honest listening help each person hear their own inner guidance and reconnect what they do with who they are.
courses.price: All-inclusive package (tuition, lodging and meals); price depends on accommodation and is shown at registration

courses.title: Meditation, Movement, Mystery
courses.description: A loosely structured, mostly sociable retreat with meditation teacher and writer Jeff Warren, moving between seated practice, movement, sharing and time on the land. The focus is on the core skills of concentration, clarity, equanimity and care, with a nature-based guest facilitator and a closing dance party.
courses.price: All-inclusive package (tuition, lodging and meals); price depends on accommodation and is shown at registration

courses.title: Reclaiming the Feminine Elements
courses.description: Métis performer and teacher Andrea Menard leads a five-day exploration of the sacred feminine through the four elements of the medicine wheel: earth, wind, water and fire. Ritual, song, creative expression and honest self-enquiry are used to meet each element as an inner quality. Open to all genders.
courses.price: All-inclusive package (tuition, lodging and meals); price depends on accommodation and is shown at registration

courses.title: Dance of Connection
courses.description: A participatory movement retreat with Bettina Rothe in which the group dances every day, indoors and outside, using rhythm as a way into presence, connection and belonging. No dance experience is needed, only curiosity about the body and willingness to take part.
courses.price: From $1,788 CAD (commuter) to $4,285 CAD (private oceanview cabin), all-inclusive early-booking prices

courses.title: Reclaim Your Mind: Finding Rest and Play in a Wired World
courses.description: A five-day immersion with mindfulness teacher and author Jay Vidyarthi on changing our relationship with phones and screens. Simple, low-effort meditation skills, time in nature and practical habits help participants notice how devices pull at attention and choose more freely how to use them.
courses.price: All-inclusive package (tuition, lodging and meals); price depends on accommodation and is shown at registration

courses.title: Morning Yoga, Tai Chi and Movement Classes
courses.description: Hour-long early-morning classes on the Cortes Island campus most days of the season, open to guests and drop-in visitors: a gentle vinyasa yoga class that begins with breath awareness, and a flowing tai chi practice taught as moving meditation. Mats and props are provided.

free_resources.title: Hollyhock on YouTube
free_resources.description: Around 250 free videos from Hollyhock: recorded talks and conversations with visiting teachers, short films about the island campus and its garden, and glimpses of past programmes.
